xBRIEFInfo.description: Actor sort by video count is O(n^2)

plan.title: Sorting actors by video count blocks the UI and has crashed

narratives.Overview: Sorting 1,300+ actors by video count takes a very long time, cannot be scrolled during, and has crashed. Root cause is identified and quantified; this is not a spike.
narratives.Problem:
ActorGridView.assetsCount(for:) (ActorGridView.swift:591) scans EVERY asset and allocates a Set per asset. It is called from inside the sort comparator (ActorGridView.swift:259), twice per comparison.

1,335 actors produce ~13,900 comparisons, so ~27,800 calls, each scanning 1,346 assets: approximately 37 MILLION asset inspections plus a Set allocation per asset per call.

It runs synchronously on the main thread inside a SwiftUI computed property, which is why the screen cannot scroll while it works.
narratives.Action:
Precompute the counts once per data change into a [String: Int], then let the comparator read it in O(1).

One pass over 1,346 assets, incrementing per actor and per AKA. Cost falls from ~37 million inspections to ~1,346 - roughly four orders of magnitude.

Deliberately NOT a background queue, progress spinner or concurrency change. Those treat the symptom; the work should simply not exist.
narratives.Constraint:
AKA-matched videos must still be counted. The fix must not quietly change any displayed number.

The same shape of mistake exists in the .age, .dateAdded and .rating comparators - each does a dictionary lookup per comparison. Far cheaper, but fix them in the same pass.
narratives.Risk: Stale counts if the map is not rebuilt when assets or profiles change. The invalidation point matters more than the map itself.
narratives.Test:
T1 - the precomputed count equals the current per-actor computation for every actor, including AKA-matched videos. This is what stops the fix silently changing the numbers.
T2 - sorting 1,335 actors completes within an asserted main-thread budget, not an eyeballed one.
narratives.Source: Spec R1. Code: ActorGridView.swift:259, :591. Library scale measured 2026-08-03: 1,335 actors, 1,346 videos.

items.title: Build a per-actor video count map in one pass, including AKA matches
Comparator reads the map instead of calling assetsCount
Invalidate/rebuild the map when assets or profiles change
Apply the same treatment to .age, .dateAdded and .rating comparators
T1 equivalence test against the current computation
